posts.name: Elcarp
posts.cooked: Is it allowed to use Omnitron, Onmitron IV, and Omnitron X all in the same game? My daughter and I tried this, and we had troubles deciding what to do with cards that affected drone cards and components, as all three have cards of the same type. For example, Converyor Panels is a component from the environment deck that states "Drone cards are immune to melee damage." Would this apply to all drones from all three versions, or just the one from the environment deck. Then there's the S-83 Assault Drone from the villian deck, that deals x melee damage, where x = the number of drones in play plus 1. Would that apply to all drones, or just the drones from the villian deck?

posts.name: AlexxKay
posts.cooked:
Looking at it from a game designer's perspective, there are clear signs that Omnitron-X and Omnitron-IV were both built with the explicit intention of having interesting interactions with other Omnitrons.

See also Grand Warlord Voss and the Dok'Thorath Capitol.  The keywords Minion and Thorathian suddenly become much... denser when both are in play.

By contrast, the game designer does not sanction having multiple variants of the same hero deck in play at once.  If you want Legacy, Young Legacy and Old Legacy all in the same game, you need to use house rules (and have extra copies of the Legacy deck!).  You can, of course, have any one version of Legacy go up against Iron Legacy, just like you can have Visionary fight The Dreamer.

posts.cooked:
Elcarp:

That makes sense. What about my first question? Is it even allowed officially to have them in the same game, or is it akin to multiple of the same hero? Technically all three are the same being, just different incarnations of him.

Whatever the timeline fiction says, the real restriction is that you can only have one copy of a given DECK in a game.  As long as the 'alternate' version has its own unique deck (not just a variant Hero card), it's allowed.

The one cool thing that allowing multiple versions of a deck with variants would be the "Flash of Two Worlds" aspect, where the Legacies team up to fight La Capitan or whoever. It would make for a cool story, but I'm not sure how fun the game is.

Limiting the "Limiteds" sounds like a good balance. I get why the restriction is there, and I'd only be interested in it as a "story mission" or some kind of goofy house-rules match.

It's like attacks which hit "a target" can hit anything, even the person using the attack, and stuff which occurs "at the start/end of each turn" do so at that point in every turn, not just that deck's turn (missed this for a while with that card in Fanatic's deck…Divine Focus, I think? Every turn, not just hers!) :D.
